name: Fei Yu-ching
description:
'''Fei Yu-ching''' ({{lang-zh|t=費玉清|s=费玉清|hp=Fèi Yùqīng|first=t}}; born '''Chang Yen-ting'''; 17 July 1955) is a Taiwanese retired singer and former television host. He is best known for his distinctive singing voice, formal stage attire, and characteristic upward-facing singing posture in [[Mandopop]]. His best-known songs include "[[Yi Jian Mei (song)|Yi Jian Mei]]" (一翦梅), "Good Night Song" (晚安曲), "Meng Tuo Ling" (夢駝鈴), and "[[Ode to the Republic of China]]" (中華民國頌). 

Born in [[Taipei]], Taiwan, to a [[Waishengren|''waishengren'']] family, Fei began his career in 1973 and initially gained recognition for performing patriotic songs and traditional-style Mandarin ballads. He received the Male Singing Performer Award at the 19th [[Golden Bell Awards]] in 1984, and his album ''Good Night Song'' won a [[Golden Melody Awards|Golden Melody Award]] in 1996. During the 1990s, he expanded into television hosting, appearing alongside his brother [[Chang Fei]] on the variety program ''The Fantastic Brothers'' (龍兄虎弟), for which they won a Golden Bell Award in 1995. He won two additional Golden Bell Awards for television hosting in 1997 and 2005.

In 2006, Fei collaborated with singer-songwriter [[Jay Chou]] on the duet "Faraway" (千里之外). He continued recording, appearing on television, and performing concerts throughout the 2000s and 2010s. In September 2018, Fei announced his retirement from the entertainment industry due to the deaths of his parents. He concluded his 46-year singing career with a 37-concert farewell tour. He performed his final concert at the [[Taipei Arena]] on 7 November 2019.
